reviewed_visual_evidence.notes: Pit straight and Sainte-Dévote: Stands and stone/pink apartment tiers frame the uphill opening. Pit/service bars, marina edge, Armco and high mesh fence. Sainte-Dévote needs its opening/runoff access, not a solid urban wall.

Beau Rivage, Massenet and Casino: Steep uphill street with continuous inhabited facades, stepped retaining walls, trees and upper hillside apartments. Casino/Hotel de Paris geometry needs targeted review; overview has no reliable close view.

Mirabeau, Fairmont and Portier: Tight descending sequence between pale hotel/apartment walls and planted terraces; palms and close red/white kerbs. Fairmont compound is a broad terraced hotel, not a freestanding tower. Bridge/overhang near hairpin seen, exact assignment needs registration.

Mirabeau, Fairmont and Portier: Tight descending sequence between pale hotel/apartment walls and planted terraces; palms and close red/white kerbs. Fairmont compound is a broad terraced hotel, not a freestanding tower. Bridge/overhang near hairpin seen, exact assignment needs registration.
Start/pit straight with close left pit building and right harbour grandstands. Earlier tunnel association was incorrect; this image is not a tunnel source.

Nouvelle chicane and harbour edge: Harbour yachts, masts and large moored vessel silhouettes, steep apartment-covered slopes behind. Exposed pale rock cliff/retaining wall on inland side; red/white chicane islands and close Armco.

rocher_and_mirabeau_surface_correction.cause: Monaco shared generator supplies Runoff as default scenery material. Actual RGE bare-earth Rocher hillside and narrow Mirabeau interstreet skin therefore read as asphalt. No terrain height correction is needed. Missing mapped crest houses and woodland compounded the bare slope.

2550_600_350.interpretation: True north Rocher ground; outside mapped woodland near cliff/wood transition, not BeauRivage verge.

diagnostic_pixels.1335_400_300: Scenery triangle bridges narrow upper1276/lower1353 street edges, not road underside. Concrete retaining support exists behind the skin.

rocher_and_mirabeau_surface_correction.landcover_geometry: Mapped woods replace underlying asphalt and support251 reconstructed5.5–10m broadleaf trees, no palms. Limestone applies to unplanted existing12m cells within60m of mapped cliff where IGN ground>8m and gradient>=.2, plus registered Mirabeau interstreet strip. Cliff buffer/slope threshold are original visual classification estimates, not surveyed geology boundaries. Roads, protection, paths, water and actual building footprints are excluded.
rocher_and_mirabeau_surface_correction.scenery_street_exclusion: Avenue de la Porte Neuve165636031 retains its existing asphalt through an estimated6m width supported by its two-lane tag; no racing-road or native collision edits. Below-ground tunnels do not remove above-ground vegetation.
rocher_and_mirabeau_surface_correction.architecture: Twelve actual mapped Rocher crest footprints. Tagged3/4 storeys retained with shared3.4m storey conversion. Untagged houses estimated3storeys. Narrow recessed openings, original dark shutter geometry, cream plaster and footprint-clipped terracotta hip roofs distinguish historic houses from modern office grids. Individual facade colours, shutter positions and roof pitches remain reconstructed. Chapel separately plain masonry, timber entrance and pale stone doorframe; estimated10.5m eave, no invented office floors or tower.
